questions.q: Under the first law of thermodynamics, what happens to energy?
a: It is never created or destroyed, only transferred
It grows every time work is performed
It disappears once it has been used up
It can be generated from motion alone
questions.why: Lesson 1 says energy cannot be created or destroyed; it only changes form.

questions.q: What does the summary say our bodies do while we sit still and think?
a: Keep working and using energy to stay alive
Store energy for later without spending any
Create new energy out of concentration
Shut down most energy use until we move
questions.why: Lesson 1 points out that the body is still hard at work even when motionless.

questions.q: Why are there many more plants than animals on earth?
a: Energy gets scarcer the further a creature is from sunlight
Animals need far less energy than plants to survive
Plants convert energy more slowly than animals do
Most animals cannot digest plant matter efficiently
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that organisms far from solar radiation struggle to get energy.

questions.q: Which energy source does the summary call the cleanest way forward?
a: Nuclear power
Solar power
Wind power
Hydropower
questions.why: Lesson 3 calls nuclear the cleanest option, though it remains debated.

questions.q: What two unresolved problems with nuclear plants does the summary name?
a: Terrorist attacks and waste disposal
Cost overruns and public protests
Meltdown risk and water use
Fuel shortages and land use
questions.why: Lesson 3 mentions protecting plants from attacks and disposing of waste.
